questions.stem: What is the original source of energy for most ecosystems?
questions.explanation: The Sun is the original source of energy for almost all ecosystems. Producers (green plants and algae) convert light energy from the Sun into chemical energy through photosynthesis, which then passes through the food chain.

questions.stem: Approximately what percentage of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next?
questions.explanation: Only about 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next. The remaining 90% is lost, mainly as heat through respiration, but also through movement, excretion, and parts not being eaten or digested.

questions.stem: What is the main way energy is lost between trophic levels?
questions.explanation: The main way energy is lost between trophic levels is through respiration, which releases energy as heat. Organisms use energy from respiration for movement, maintaining body temperature, and other life processes.

questions.stem: Why are food chains usually limited to four or five trophic levels?

options.text: Because predators refuse to eat other predators
Because energy is lost at each level, leaving insufficient energy to support further levels
Because there are not enough species

questions.explanation: Food chains are limited because energy is lost at each trophic level. By the fourth or fifth level, there is not enough energy remaining to support another trophic level. This is why top predators are relatively rare.

options.text: The total mass of organisms at each trophic level
The number of organisms at each trophic level
The height of organisms at each trophic level
The age of organisms at each trophic level

questions.explanation: A pyramid of biomass shows the total mass of living material (biomass) at each trophic level. It is generally pyramid-shaped because biomass decreases at higher trophic levels due to energy losses.

questions.stem: How can the efficiency of energy transfer be calculated?

options.text: (Energy in at current level / Energy in at previous level) x 100

questions.explanation: Efficiency of energy transfer is calculated as (energy available at one trophic level / energy available at the previous trophic level) x 100. This typically gives a value of around 10%.

questions.stem: Why is energy flow described as a one-way process, unlike the cycling of matter?

options.text: Because organisms only eat in one direction
Because the Sun only shines in one direction
Because producers cannot use energy from consumers
Because energy is converted to heat and lost to the environment, and cannot be recycled

questions.explanation: Energy flow is one-way because energy is ultimately converted to heat through respiration and lost to the environment. Unlike matter (carbon, nitrogen), which can be recycled, heat energy cannot be reused by organisms.
